Alex.confusing: The vote math was hard to track, especially how a thrown card from a dead player still counts as a card in the pile but not as a vote. The consolation return rule was also easy to misread.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when my Turkey visit left me unaffected and the table converged on Drew from a single Hawk egg. Watching the claims collide over who was Tit was the best part.
Alex.change: Make the Storyteller's reports clearer about which claims are verifiable, so players can tell a real egg from an unverified story.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I threw both of my Kings at Ellis, which lost them and left me as the eggsecuted target. I would throw low cards and keep my high cards, since Ellis was only one vote and my Hawk claim had already exposed me.

Blair.confusing: The dead-player rules were unclear: a dead player still throws and banks cards, but I couldn't tell whether that was worth a full throw when my team's win was uncertain. Also, Blair's Hawk egg counted as proof on Drew even though Hawks are the only role that gains from a target, which made the chain easy to misread.
Blair.fun: Round 2 turned on the Tit and Kookaburra claims clashing, with Drew and Ellis each accusing the other, and the table converged on Drew as Meowfia.
Blair.change: Make it clearer whether a Hawk's egg means the target is Meowfia, and show each player's visit count at dawn so claims are easier to check.
Blair.regret: In round 3, after Blair was winked, I threw all five cards at Casey while dead, and most of them were discarded when Farm lost. I would throw one or two low cards instead and keep my high cards as a floor.

Casey.confusing: The Sphinx's night action was unclear to me: naming a role gave me the holder's identity, but I couldn't tell how that would matter during the day. Hawk egg rules (gaining only from Meowfia targets) also took a while to pin down.
Casey.fun: Blair collapsing mid-day after my Mouser visit, and the table scrambling to read it as a Wink, was the most fun moment.
Casey.change: I would make role claims harder to fake, perhaps by giving each player a verifiable egg trail, so one convenient nest change can't back up a false story.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw three cards at Alex, a Farm player, which was wasted. I should have thrown at Ellis, the other Meowfia, and kept my high cards.

Drew.confusing: The Hawk mechanic was hard to track: a Hawk gains an egg only when its target is Meowfia, and the Hawk's own nest stays flat, so day claims about egg gains were easy to misread.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when I was secretly the Sphinx and Blair claimed a Hawk hit on me while my nest stayed flat, and the table spent the day arguing over who was lying.
Drew.change: I would make egg changes clearer, for example by showing each dawn egg change publicly, so players can check claims without guessing.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw my high cards at Blair, a Farm Hawk, to pull votes off myself. I would have thrown lower cards and kept my 13 and 9 for my score.

Ellis.confusing: The Sphinx and Mouser night reveals were hard to track, and I never knew whether my Meowfia partner was alive or who it was. The one-of-each-animal rule also made it hard to judge claims like two Kookaburras.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when I was the Sphinx and learned the Farm roles, then steered the table with a false Kookaburra claim while Blair collapsed to the Wink.
Ellis.change: Show each player's team as a public fact when a Meowfia player dies or wins, so the table can tell who has a partner left.
Ellis.regret: In Round 1 I threw my Wild at Casey, who was my Meowfia partner, which helped get my own side eliminated. I would stay quiet or throw at Blair, the Farm Hawk, instead.

Finley.confusing: The Hawk and Kookaburra "confused" mechanics were hard to read, since my own dawn report could be off and I couldn't tell when it was. Also, the Storyteller's note that a Hawk gains only from Meowfia targets made the egg evidence harder to interpret.
Finley.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: Blair's Hawk egg pointed at Casey, the table converged, and Casey was eggsecuted with an 8-vote landslide. Watching the Tit/Kookaburra/Turkey claims collide across the table was the highlight.
Finley.change: I would make role claims and confusion more transparent, so the table can tell a true Hawk or Kookaburra report from a confused one.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I threw two cards at Casey and helped push Alex's elimination indirectly by piling votes on the wrong target, which let Meowfia win. I'd have checked Alex's Hawk claim against Ellis's reported nest more carefully before calling the vote.

review.title: The Wink Flips It
review.headline: Farm solved two rounds easily, then a Meowfia pair framed the Hawk and won.
review.summary: Rounds 1 and 2 were quick Farm wins. A Hawk egg named the Meowfia and everyone piled on. Blair banked big and led after round 2. In round 3 Casey winked the Owl Blair, then both Meowfia threw at Alex. The Farm split its votes and Alex was eggsecuted. Ellis and Casey took first and second, and the Farm team that was right all day lost.

rounds.recap: Blair's Hawk hit Casey, the Sphinx, and gained an egg. Alex's Falcon report backed it. Ellis posed as an Owl but the table still threw at Casey. Farm won and Blair banked 11 points.
Blair the Hawk gained an egg on Drew. Drew and Ellis both claimed Tit, which exposed Drew. Blair, Casey and Ellis threw heavily and Drew was eggsecuted. Farm banked large scores.

Alex the Hawk gained on Ellis. Casey winked Owl Blair and admitted it. Both Meowfia threw at Alex while the Farm split votes between Casey and Ellis. Alex was eggsecuted. Meowfia won and Ellis took first.

highlights.text: Drew claimed Tit, Ellis claimed it too, and the unique-role clash decided the vote.
Blair collapsed mid-day to Casey's Wink, and Casey then openly admitted it.
Farm split its throws between Casey and Ellis, so Meowfia's focused votes on Alex won the round.
Blair's Hawk egg on Casey gave Farm a clean, early answer.

confusions.what: Argued Blair's Hawk hit should have changed Drew's nest. A Hawk only gains for itself.
Said a Hawk visit would have changed Ellis's nest. It would not.
Said Blair's story was false because Casey's nest was unchanged. A Hawk's target is unaffected.
Claimed Owl, but with Blair as the only Hawk this was an easy bluff for others to doubt. Some players also suspected Ellis's Owl claim was impossible.
Threw only one card at Casey while Meowfia piled on Alex.

worked: Hawk gains an egg on a Meowfia target. It gives one hard, checkable fact each round.
Unique animals make double claims (the two Tits, the two Kookaburras) detectable and decisive.
The Mouser's Wink creates a real mid-day swing. Meowfia can attack the best-informed Farm player.
Throw counts are public, so a vote split on the Farm side is visible and punished.
problems: Hawk is too strong. Farm solved rounds 1 and 2 with one egg and no real doubt. Consider letting a Hawk gain only on a hit, with a cost on a miss, or reducing how clearly the result reads.
Early CAW CAW calls ended rounds 1 and 3 quickly. Meowfia had little time to bluff. Consider requiring all 4 beats or more callers.
Score runaway: Blair got 11 then 17 points. Banking high cards when Farm wins makes round 1 and 2 leaders hard to catch. Check the point swing against the first-place-only goal.
In round 3 a Meowfia win came from Farm splitting votes between two targets, not from deduction. The rules for two Meowfia and ties favour a focused Meowfia bloc.
Players kept misreading the Hawk and Tit rules. Reports should state the Hawk result plainly, like 'target was Meowfia'.
